bull.b: The combination of low-20s constant-currency growth and margins targeted at 65% gross and roughly 20% adjusted EBITDA indicates scalable demand and operating leverage. If achieved, these targets support reinvestment in products, retail and global expansion while strengthening earnings durability.

Rapid DTC growth increases control over brand presentation, customer relationships and pricing, while shifting mix toward a channel that captures more of the retail economics. A larger DTC base can therefore support durable margins and reduce reliance on wholesale distribution over time.

A substantial net cash position and strong recent free cash flow give On flexibility to fund innovation, stores and international growth without depending heavily on external financing. This financial capacity also improves resilience if demand or working-capital needs become more volatile.

bear.b: Slower wholesale growth, particularly in the Americas, shows that parts of the retail partner channel are not converting demand as strongly as DTC. Continued promotional pressure could constrain volume, complicate inventory planning and make consolidated growth more dependent on direct channels.

Inventory growth materially above the broader sales cadence requires disciplined sell-through and replenishment management, especially while wholesale orders are being calibrated. If products move more slowly than planned, working capital could remain tied up and promotional activity could pressure future margins.

Higher U.S. import tariffs create an external cost pressure that can weigh on margins or require pricing and sourcing responses. Because the expected refunds depend on timing and were excluded from guidance, near-term profitability and cash benefits remain uncertain.
